messages:
maria: Heads-up — this morning eu-west-gpu pool spiked into burst for ~45m and we blew through the soft burst budget. Cost alert triggered and we fell back to a 4k token model on some routes. Not catastrophic but noticeable latency increase.
kevin: link to the alert? what caused the spike — a single customer or organic traffic?
lia: alert summary from the monitor: `eu-west-gpu-pool: burst_count=1, peak_concurrent_gpus=42, reserved_capacity=32, burst_overage=10, duration=2700s` 
lia: Also saw a pattern of long sequence generations from /chat/stream for two mobile partners (sessionIDs redacted).
sre-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-17 08:12Z eu-west GPU pool burst budget exceeded. Estimated incremental GPU-hours: 7.2h. Cost delta estimate: ~$1.5k.
tomo: For context — our autoscaler currently allows burst up to +25% over reserved per-pool with no strict cooldown. That plus a wide `max_scale` on some nodegroups is what let it spike.
kevin: Can we get metrics for P95 latency and token throughput during the event? want to see SLO impact.
lia: P95 generation latency went from 180ms -> 420ms for 8s windows during peak. Token throughput per-GPU stayed ~stable; the issue was queueing across pools when fallback routing kicked in.
ops-lead: Q3 planning note: this is the kind of event that will cost us in Q4 unless we tighten guardrails. We expect holiday traffic multipliers 2.0-2.5x.
maria: Proposal: tighten burst cap to +12% per-pool, add a 15m cooldown after any burst, and enforce an absolute global cap on burst GPUs across the region (eu-west) — e.g., global_burst_max = 12 GPUs. Also add a routing priority so latency-sensitive routes don't get routed to fallback models unless all primary capacity exhausted.
tomo: I ran a small sim yesterday. With +12% and cooldown 15m our tail probability of >2x cost overrun drops from 7% -> 1.6% for traffic traces (sample: mobile partners + organic).
kevin: Sounds reasonable. Need to check impact on customer latency for peak workloads. Could we do a canary in eu-west with two pools: pool-a (tight guardrails) and pool-b (current settings) and split traffic 10/90?
lia: I can run the canary and collect p50/p95/p99 plus token-hours. Suggest 72h canary during low-traffic window.
sre-bot: ACTION created: #INC-2026-118 — run autoscale canary in eu-west. Assignee: lia. Deadline: 2026-03-24.
ops-lead: Also need forecasting update: adjust GPU-hours model to include burst attenuation factor and a seasonal multiplier. Lia/tomo, can you both update the forecast sheet with the new guardrail assumptions so finance can re-run reserved capacity proposals?
maria: I'll update rollout runbook to include the new fallback priority rules, and the rollback criteria (cost delta > 30% or p99 latency > 800ms).
tomo: snippet of the suggested autoscaler policy (simplified):
```yaml
autoscalingPolicy:
  perPoolBurstPercent: 12
  perPoolCooldownSeconds: 900
  regionGlobalBurstMax: 12
  priorityRouting:
    - route: "/chat/stream"
      minReserve: 0.95
      allowFallback: false
    - route: "/embeddings"
      minReserve: 0.7
      allowFallback: true
```
kevin: Nice. Also add a budget tracker that emits an alert at 75% of burst budget so we don't get surprised.
lia: will add an alert and a dashboard tile for token-hours burned in burst vs steady state.
ops-lead: For forecasting: if Q4 multiplier 2.3x and we allow +12% burst, the recommended reserved pool increase is roughly +40 GPUs for eu-west to keep tail latency in check (ballpark). Finance should look at commit pricing vs on-demand burst.
maria: Agreed. Next steps: 1) lia runs the 72h canary (start Tue 03:00Z), 2) tomo and lia update forecast sheet, 3) kevin adds budget-alert and dashboard, 4) I update runbook and schedule a post-canary review.
kevin: I'll add the budget alert now — tag me if you want to tweak thresholds.
lia: I'll post canary results as a short thread with metrics and logs.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup: If anyone sees unexpected behavior during the canary ping #oncall immediately.
kevin: ack.
ops-lead: closing loop: please add estimated GPU-hours delta in the canary ticket so finance can estimate cost impact quickly.
maria: noted — adding to #INC-2026-118.
